references.text: The same command to bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water, as part of the priestly consecration ritual.
Describes how Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet with water from the bronze basin before entering the tent of meeting.
The fulfillment of this command where Moses actually brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
The cleansing ritual for the Levites that includes sprinkling the water of purification over them.
The New Testament refers to the Old Testament cleansing with clean water as a foreshadowing of spiritual cleansing in Christ.
Distinguishes between the consecrating wash at the entrance and the ongoing washing of hands and feet before service.
Complementary steps in consecration: washing for purity and anointing for sanctification.
The washing as an essential component within the overall consecration process.
A summary emphasizing that washing is a necessary part of total obedience.
